contents.name: II.1 Definitions of H^p(D) and H^p(dt); quasi-norm for p<1
II.1 Completeness of H^p for 0<p<infinity (Theorem 1.3)
contents.reason: Complete quasi-Banach space theory is not used by any item of this pair; the scaffold needs only the (quasi-)norm axioms, radial-mean monotonicity and the containment H^q in H^p, recorded elsewhere.

contents.name: II.2 Blaschke condition from Jensen formula for a nonzero H^p function
II.2 Normalized factor estimate |1-b_n(z)| <= (1-|z_n|)(1+|z|)/(1-|z|) and normal convergence of the product
II.2 Argument |B/B_n(0)| <= (1/2pi) integral |B| giving |B| = 1 a.e. on the circle
II.2 Theorem 2.3: f = Bg with the H^p norms of g and f equal
II.2 Theorem 2.4: log-mean and least-harmonic-majorant characterization of arbitrary Blaschke products
contents.reason: Garnett printed pp.53-54 covers finite or infinite Blaschke products. This additional iff characterization by vanishing limiting log mean or zero least harmonic majorant is not required by CA-HP2; thm-blaschke-product-boundary-values-and-zeros proves the commissioned unimodularity using tails, without asserting this characterization.

contents.name: II.3 Theorem 3.1: nontangential limits, maximal bound, boundary isometry and L^p convergence for 0<p<infinity
contents.evidence: Clauses(a)-(c) are fully proved under CC by bounded-quotient boundary data, Poisson-Jensen envelope, explicit uniform integrability and Fourier identification. Proof step6.1 independently proves the included strong maximal bound with constant24^(1/p)(A+1)^(4/p) for finitep, and the infinity bound.

contents.name: II.3 Corollary 3.2: boundary characterization of H^p functions for p >= 1
II.3 Corollary 3.3: density of the smooth classes A_N in H^p
contents.reason: The half-plane density class A_N is a device of the source own transfer argument between H^p(dt) and H^p(D); this pair works on the disc throughout and needs no approximation class.

contents.name: II.3 Corollary 3.4: H^p(D) versus H^p(dt) and the least harmonic majorant (3.4)
contents.reason: The conformal transfer between the disc and the half-plane is not used in this pair; all items are stated and proved on the disc.

contents.name: II.4 Corollary 4.3: H^p intersect L^r subset H^r
contents.evidence: Garnett printed p.64 Corollary4.3. Hp is contained in N+ by def-smirnov-class-on-the-disc using Poisson-Jensen inequality; theorem steps1.1/2.1/2.2/3.1 yield Hr membership and exact norm from an Lr boundary datum. This covers the full regularity upgrade, including r=infinity.

contents.name: II.3 Theorem 3.6 (first half): an H^1 function is the Poisson integral of its boundary values
II.3 Theorem 3.6 (second half): an analytic Poisson integral has an absolutely continuous measure
II.3 Lemma 3.7: vanishing Fourier transform of H^1 boundary functions
II.3 Theorem 3.8 and its proof: a measure with vanishing negative Fourier coefficients has analytic Poisson integral, expanded as a power series
II.4 Theorem 4.4: necessity of log-integrability for nonzero Hardy boundary moduli
contents.evidence: Garnett printed p.64 Theorem4.4. Steps2.1/3.1 prove the positive/negative logarithmic parts integrable and step4.1 gives nonvanishing almost everywhere. The sufficiency direction is separately included under lem-outer-function-properties.

contents.name: II.4 Theorem 4.4: h in L^p with log h in L^1 iff h = |f^*| a.e. for some f in H^p
II.4 Outer function (4.5) f = e^{u+iv}, u = P[log h], determined by h up to a unimodular constant
II.4 Theorem 4.6: equivalent characterizations of outer functions
II.4 Corollaries 4.7 and 4.8: 1/f in H^r forces f outer; Re f >= 0 forces f outer
contents.reason: These sufficient criteria for outer functions are not used by any item of the pair; the factorization is obtained instead from the boundary modulus and the Poisson-Jensen inequality.

contents.name: II.5 Theorem 5.1: f in N iff log^+|f| has a Poisson-integral majorant
II.5 (5.1) and the least-harmonic-majorant remark after Theorem 5.1: bounded radial log^+ means iff log^+|f| has a harmonic majorant
II.5 Lemma 5.2: Blaschke factorization and membership in N
II.5 Theorem 5.3: nontangential limits and log-integrability of boundary values in N
II.5 Inequality (5.5): log|f| <= P[log|f^*|] for H^p functions, and the point-mass counterexample
II.5 Definition of N^+ by the boundary-log condition (c), with the quotient description
II.5 Theorem 5.4: equivalences for N^+ and N^+ intersect L^p = H^p
II.5 Theorem 5.5: canonical factorization of N-functions
II.5 Corollary 5.6: the factor S_2 is trivial iff f lies in N^+
II.5 Corollary 5.7: unique factorization f = C B S F for f in H^p
II.5 Corollary 5.8: f in N^+ lies in H^p iff its outer factor does
II.5 Singular functions S_j from positive singular measures and their properties (i)-(iv)
II.6 Inner-function definition and every inner function = e^{ic} B S
II.6 Theorem 6.1: analytic continuation of Blaschke products across the circle off accumulation points
contents.reason: Boundary regularity of Blaschke products away from accumulation points is not needed: the pair uses only a.e. unimodular boundary values, proved by the mean-value argument of Section 2.

contents.name: II.6 Theorem 6.2: behaviour of a singular function at the support of its measure
contents.reason: Quantitative divergence of singular functions at their singular set is not used; the pair needs only |S^*| = 1 a.e. for singular measures and the point-mass illustration on the companion page.

contents.name: II.6 Theorem 6.3: analyticity or continuity across an arc passes to the factors
contents.reason: Boundary regularity transfer across arcs belongs to the later study of inner functions and is not used by any proof in this pair.

contents.name: II.7 Beurling theorem on shift-invariant subspaces
contents.reason: Beurling invariant-subspace theorem belongs to the operator-theoretic development of H^2 and is explicitly excluded by the design; model spaces and shift-invariant subspaces are a later track.

contents.name: I.5 Lemma 5.4: singular finite circle measures have Poisson integrals tending nontangentially to zero almost everywhere
contents.evidence: Complete available OCR proof read at printedpp29-30; independently proved here under CC by compact singular-carrier approximation and the published finite-circle weak maximal estimate. No closure-of-small-open-set assertion or full-AC differentiation supplier is used.

contents.name: II.3 Theorem3.1 bounded holomorphic case: independent countable-choice Taylor/Fourier boundary representation
contents.evidence: Full analytic Fatou claim retained separately; this special lemma proves the bounded case from Taylor uniform convergence, radial Parseval, CC Fourier Riesz-Fischer and CC Poisson Fatou, without the full-AC bounded-harmonic representation.

contents.name: I.3 Theorem3.1 Poisson uniqueness and II.3 circle Fourier coefficients: finite complex circle measure uniqueness under CC
contents.evidence: Complete availableI.3 theorem/proof and the printedII.3p57 coefficient discussion read. Local proof uses uniform trigonometric density, a regular-variation compact/open cutoff, and the uniform Poisson series; it proves Fourier and Poisson uniqueness without a general harmonic measure-existence theorem.

The design locator (Srivastava §§2.4, 2.6-2.7, 3.1-3.10) is the numbering of an earlier version of these same notes; the current MA650 version carries the same material at §§4.4, 4.6-4.7, 5.6-5.11 and 6.2-6.4, which is the locator recorded here. contents.name: 5.1 Properties of H^p spaces (radial means, containment, quasi-norm)
5.1 Monotonicity of radial p-means and the containment H^q(D) in H^p(D)
5.5 Identification of H^p(D) with H^p(T) (Theorem 5.8)
5.6 Jensen formula and Jensen inequality (Lemma 5.11, Corollary 5.12)
5.6 Generalized Jensen inequality via the automorphism substitution
5.7 Boundary uniqueness theorem (Corollary 5.14)
5.8 Blaschke condition (Lemma 5.17) and the Blaschke product (Lemma 5.19)
5.8 Boundary behaviour and zeros of the infinite product
5.8 F. Riesz factorization f = Bg with equal p-norms (Corollary 5.20)
5.9 Non-tangential boundary limits and Fatou theorem (Theorem 5.25, Corollary 5.26)
5.9 Herglotz representation of positive harmonic functions (Theorem 5.28)
5.10 Outer function [f] and properties (i)-(iv) (Theorem 5.27)
5.10 Singular inner functions (Theorem 5.29)
5.10 Smirnov canonical factorization (Theorem 5.32) and structure of outer functions (Theorem 5.33)
5.11 Approximation by inner functions and Blaschke products (Douglas-Rudin, Theorem 5.37)
contents.reason: Uniform approximation by inner functions belongs to the uniform-algebra theory of H^infty and is excluded by the design, which reserves model spaces and operator theory for a later pair.

contents.name: 6.2 Properties of outer functions, including the integral maximal principle
6.3 The Nevanlinna (N) and Smirnov (N+) classes
6.3 Original definition of N by bounded radial log^+ means and its equivalence with the majorant/quotient description (paragraph before Theorem 6.21)
6.3 Quotient representation of N-functions by bounded analytic functions
6.3 Boundary values and log-integrability for N
6.3 Smirnov class as bounded quotients with outer denominator
6.4 Conformally invariant framework for N and N+
contents.reason: The conformal transfer of the Nevanlinna and Smirnov classes to the half-plane is not used; every statement of this pair is formulated and proved on the unit disc.

contents.name: 6.5 Generalized Phragmen-Lindelof principle
contents.reason: The generalized Phragmen-Lindelof principle is a growth theorem beyond the scope of the commissioned claims and is not used by any item of this pair.

Riesz theorem", printed pp. 75-79: Definition 5.14, Propositions 5.15-5.17, Definition 5.18, Propositions 5.19-5.21, Theorem 5.13 and Theorem 5.22, together with the printed proof of Theorem 5.13.

contents.name: 5.4 Definitions and Propositions 5.14-5.18: extended subharmonic functions, mean property, maximum principle, radial maximal function
contents.reason: The primitive subharmonic tools are already published and actually used: modulus-power subharmonicity and Poisson modification in lem-hardy-radial-means-are-monotone, plus maximum principle in lem-nevanlinna-sup-mean-criterion. This row declines reminting the broader Ryzhik toolkit/radial-maximal definition as new local items; it does not claim those published prerequisites are unused.

contents.name: 5.4 Proposition 5.19: maximal bounds for general nonnegative subharmonic functions with bounded radial means
contents.reason: The general nonnegative-subharmonic maximal theorem is an additional toolkit claim. Current analytic Fatou uses its own CC Nevanlinna/Poisson-log/UI proof, and its ancillary analytic maximal estimate follows directly from the earlier circle weak bound and layer-cake. No assertion for arbitrary subharmonic g is needed.

contents.name: 5.4 Proposition 5.20: radial maximal function of an analytic H1 function lies in L1
contents.evidence: Proof step6.1 gives the full nontangential strong p bound at p=1 under CC; every radial point is in each aperture A>1 cone, so the radial maximal function is bounded by that integrable nontangential maximal function.

contents.name: 5.4 Proposition 5.21: an analytic H1 function is the Poisson integral of its L1 radial boundary limit
contents.evidence: Proof steps3.1 and4.1 give radial L1 convergence and Poisson identification through Taylor/Fourier coefficients, under CC; no general AC h1 measure-existence theorem is used.

contents.name: 5.4 Theorem 5.13: F. and M. Riesz theorem for measures with vanishing negative Fourier coefficients
5.4 Theorem 5.22: for analytic h^1 functions log|f| lies in L^1, so the boundary function cannot vanish on a positive-measure set
